Test a weighted combination using inverse_error to see if error-based weighting improves over simple mean given unstable ranking.
test a different weighting scheme (softmax_neg_error) on the full pool to see if it improves over mean and weighted inverse_error.
Test a robust weighted combination using inverse_error on the full pool to see if explicit weighting improves over mean.
test robust median over full pool
Try a robust DBA combination over the full pool to exploit unstable ranking and strong seasonality.
I will test a per‑horizon weighted combination using the top‑k mean per horizon handle (w5) over the full pool to see if horizon‑specific averaging improves over the robust mean.
Test a per-horizon softmax weighting on the stable pool4 to see if horizon‑specific weighting improves over the mean/median baseline, leveraging the unstable ranking and strong seasonality.
The series has unstable ranking and strong seasonality, so a per‑horizon weighted combination may capture changing strengths.
The series has strong trend and seasonality but ranking is unstable; a robust trimmed mean over the full pool may reduce influence of outlier models while keeping many models active.
test a simple mean over the smaller, more stable pool4 to see if reducing noise improves robust combination.

decision.justification: Selected 'median' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9421. Series context: trend strength 1.0 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.185); 2 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.476.
